hook.en: Newspapers say India's GDP grew 7 per cent and onion prices rose by ₹20 a kg. Where do such numbers come from, and how do we trust them?
hook.kn: ಭಾರತದ ಜಿಡಿಪಿ ಶೇ 7 ಬೆಳೆಯಿತು, ಈರುಳ್ಳಿ ಬೆಲೆ ಕೆಜಿಗೆ ₹20 ಏರಿತು ಎಂದು ಪತ್ರಿಕೆಗಳು ಹೇಳುತ್ತವೆ. ಈ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆಗಳು ಎಲ್ಲಿಂದ ಬರುತ್ತವೆ?

objectives.en: Define statistics in the plural and singular sense

narration.en: Newspapers say India's GDP grew 7 per cent and onion prices rose by ₹20 a kg. Where do such numbers come from, and how do we trust them?
narration.kn: ಭಾರತದ ಜಿಡಿಪಿ ಶೇ 7 ಬೆಳೆಯಿತು, ಈರುಳ್ಳಿ ಬೆಲೆ ಕೆಜಿಗೆ ₹20 ಏರಿತು ಎಂದು ಪತ್ರಿಕೆಗಳು ಹೇಳುತ್ತವೆ. ಈ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆಗಳು ಎಲ್ಲಿಂದ ಬರುತ್ತವೆ?

title.en: Statistics in the plural and singular sense

body.en: In the plural sense, statistics means numerical data: facts and figures such as the population of Karnataka or the price of rice. In the singular sense, statistics is a subject: the methods of collecting, organising, presenting, analysing and interpreting data.
body.kn: ಬಹುವಚನದಲ್ಲಿ ಸಂಖ್ಯಾಶಾಸ್ತ್ರ ಎಂದರೆ ಸಂಖ್ಯಾತ್ಮಕ ದತ್ತಾಂಶ. ಏಕವಚನದಲ್ಲಿ ಅದು ದತ್ತಾಂಶ ಸಂಗ್ರಹ, ಸಂಘಟನೆ, ನಿರೂಪಣೆ, ವಿಶ್ಲೇಷಣೆ ಮತ್ತು ವ್ಯಾಖ್ಯಾನದ ವಿಧಾನಗಳು.

points.en: Singular: methods (collection → organisation → presentation → analysis → interpretation)

title.en: On the board: Two meanings of statistics

say.en: In the plural sense, statistics means numbers: facts and figures.
In the singular sense, statistics is a subject: the methods we use on data.
Data are of two kinds. Quantitative data are measured in numbers.
Qualitative data describe attributes like gender or literacy that cannot be measured.
Statistics are aggregates, numerically expressed, comparable and collected for a purpose.

text.en: One isolated figure is not statistics

body.en: Quantitative data can be measured in numbers, like income, age or marks. Qualitative data describe attributes that cannot be measured, like gender, religion or honesty. Statistics as data are aggregates of facts, numerically expressed, collected for a purpose and comparable.

problem.en: Sort into quantitative and qualitative: (i) weight of students, (ii) colour of eyes, (iii) number of rooms in a house, (iv) literacy status (literate / illiterate).

steps.en: (i) Weight is measured in kg: quantitative.
(ii) Eye colour is an attribute: qualitative.
(iii) Number of rooms is counted: quantitative.
(iv) Literate or not is an attribute: qualitative.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. Sort into quantitative and qualitative: (i) weight of students, (ii) colour of eyes, (iii) number of rooms in a house, (iv) literacy status (literate / illiterate).

body.en: The singular sense of statistics follows five stages in order: Collection, Organisation, Presentation, Analysis, Interpretation.
